_what: How a player lead becomes a person.
_ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-08: if a man qualifies under the standing rule he IS promoted. No batch approval. The rule has already answered, and making him approve each batch turns a rule into a queue -- and the queue only grows as documents come in.
_the_rule: A person is someone who PLAYED, COACHED OR OFFICIATED at least one season. A player named on a ROSTER for a club-season the archive HOLDS qualifies. So does a man named in the caption to a TEAM PHOTOGRAPH, under the conditions in `_team_photograph_ruling` -- and under those conditions only.
_what_still_comes_to_ryan: What the rule REFUSES or flags as AMBIGUOUS. A man named only in a transaction or a camp list; a lead whose evidence kind the route does not know; and a name more than one held person carries. Those are judgements the rule cannot make and they are reported, never promoted. A team photograph WAS on this list until 2026-09-08 and is now ruled -- see `_team_photograph_ruling`.
_no_scope_key: There was an in_scope_stores / in_scope_club_seasons pair here and it is deliberately gone. A scope key is how a standing rule quietly becomes a queue again.
_refuse_by_default: An evidence kind this route does not know is refused, not promoted. A new lead shape is not a roster until somebody says it is.

_the_property: the evidence is the caption to a TEAM PHOTOGRAPH, not a photograph of something else
the club-season is one the archive HOLDS
_team_photograph_ruling._all_three_or_nothing: A caption alone is not enough. A man named in a photograph of something other than his club's team picture is not covered, and neither is a club-season the archive does not hold. The three conditions are checked as a property in promote_players.qualify() and again in src/gate_team_photograph_promotions.py; neither names a man.
_team_photograph_ruling._why: The twelve Pacific Coast Wildcats men failed not because they did not play but because PFA's box scores only see men who STARTED, and no source ever gave that club a roster. They were excluded by a gap in the evidence, not by evidence of absence. A man in uniform, in the team picture, named by the club's own opponent's programme, has a stronger claim to membership than most of what places men on 1920s clubs.
_team_photograph_ruling._the_predicate_does_not_move: `programme.team_photograph` is NOT roster membership and does not become it. The distinction survives the promotion: the man becomes a person, and the claim keeps saying exactly what it said -- that he was photographed with this club, not that he played. A promotion under this ruling must never write a roster_membership claim, and the gate checks that as its own property.
_team_photograph_ruling._what_is_still_refused: `boxscore_lineup`, `transaction` and `training_camp` are unchanged and still refused. Signed is not rostered; a camp list is who was invited; and a boxscore lead means the man did not resolve, which is an identity question, not a promotion.

_roster_evidence_kinds._what: The evidence kinds that ARE a roster. promote_players.py reads this list; it used to type it, which is the classification-by-string pattern this archive keeps meeting -- a vocabulary in code cannot be ruled on, only edited.
_roster_evidence_kinds._refuse_by_default: Anything not on this list is refused BY NAME. The refusal is what makes the declaration mean anything: the alternative is that any ingest can widen what counts as roster evidence by naming its own lead shape something new.
_roster_evidence_kinds.printed_roster: RULED BY RYAN, 2026-09-09: a printed roster is a roster. A squad list printed in a NAMED PUBLISHED WORK and attributed to a NAMED ARCHIVE is roster evidence. It is the same object as page seven of the 1926 Bears-Tigers programme and the PFRA Annual's St. Louis Gunners rosters -- a document naming who was on a club. That it was set in 2025 from a 1905 scrapbook rather than in 1905 changes who set the type, not what the source asserts. The kind reaches the PFRA Annual's 101 leads and frankfordyellowjacketsbook.com's 103.
_roster_evidence_kinds._and_the_route_was_right_to_ask: promote_players REFUSED this kind until it was declared, and that was correct. A new lead shape must not become a roster silently. Recorded in docs/DATASET_PRECEDENTS.md.
_roster_evidence_kinds.printed_lineup: RULED BY RYAN, 2026-09-10: a printed line-up from a named contemporary newspaper is evidence the archive already accepts -- the same standing as the 1926 Bears-Tigers programme and the 1926 Pacific Coast Wildcats caption. A game account naming eleven men and their positions places those men on that club-season as surely as a squad list does, and more precisely: it names the day. AND IT IS NOT programme.probable_lineup. THAT predicate exists because the Tigers programme printed its line-up BEFORE kickoff, so a man named there was EXPECTED to start and might not have. These accounts were printed AFTER the whistle in the Bethlehem Globe-Times and the Philadelphia Public Ledger. The distinction is the printing order, and it is the whole reason these are started_a_game. A SUBSTITUTION IS NOT THIS KIND: a man who came on did not start, and the 53 substitutions are held apart under ghosts.substitution and are NOT promotable here. The kind reaches 30 men on two EFL club-seasons the club table already holds.

_a_club_season_the_archive_holds: RULED 2026-09-09, with the printed_roster ruling and forced by it: the test is whether the CLUB TABLE names the club-season, not whether the index already holds a man on it. The old test counted men in the index, which made an EMPTY club-season unfillable forever -- the first man could never be promoted onto it, because he would be the first. That is the same reasoning as the team-photograph ruling: a club-season with no roster excludes its squad by a gap in the evidence, not by evidence of absence. Frankford 1899, 1900, 1903 and 1906 are held by the club table and by nothing else, and they could not have gained a single man under the old test.
